es: Escribir el centro de una charla con énfasis: una inversión (Never have we…, Not until… did…), una regla de tres y una pregunta retórica.

teaching.en: Never have we had so many tools to communicate, yet rarely do we say anything worth remembering.
teaching.es: Nunca hemos tenido tantas herramientas para comunicarnos, y sin embargo rara vez decimos algo que valga la pena recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: Tras Never y Rarely al inicio, el auxiliar (have, do) pasa delante del sujeto (we).
segments: Never have we had so many tools to communicate,
yet rarely do we say anything worth remembering.

teaching.en: Seldom has a single phrase carried so much emphasis as those three words at the end of her speech.
teaching.es: Pocas veces una sola frase ha tenido tanto énfasis como esas tres palabras al final de su discurso.
teaching.explanationEs: Seldom se comporta como Never: va delante y el auxiliar has precede a su sujeto, a single phrase.

teaching.en: Little did the audience realise that the quiet man at the back held the tools to change the whole debate.
teaching.es: El público no sospechaba que el hombre callado del fondo tenía las herramientas para cambiar todo el debate.
teaching.explanationEs: Little did + sujeto + verbo base: did ya lleva el pasado, y la frase anuncia una sorpresa posterior.

teaching.en: Rarely does a speaker hammer home a point at the start; not until the end do listeners feel its full weight.

teaching.explanationEs: Not until + expresión de tiempo también invierte: Not until the end do listeners feel…

teaching.en: With inversion, at no point should a speech sound rehearsed, and under no circumstances should a speaker use it in every sentence.
teaching.es: Con la inversión, en ningún momento debe un discurso sonar ensayado, y bajo ninguna circunstancia debe el orador usarla en cada frase.
teaching.explanationEs: At no point y Under no circumstances también piden inversión; más de una o dos por discurso cansan.

prompt.es: Escribe el centro de una charla con inversión, regla de tres y pregunta retórica.

answer.text: Every morning, millions of us do the same thing. We turn on the tap, we wait for the water to warm up, and we let it run. Who has ever counted how many litres disappear in those two minutes? Nobody, I suspect. Never have we had so much clean water, yet rarely do we treat it with respect. Not only do we waste water at home, but we also waste the energy that heats it. Here is what I suggest: three simple habits. First, keep a bowl in the shower. Second, turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Third, repair every leak this week. Little did I know that three small habits would cut our bill by a third. Under no circumstances should we wait for a crisis, because water that has gone cannot be replaced. So tomorrow morning, turn off the tap, hold the bowl and feel what a difference it makes.
accepted: Every morning, millions of us do the same thing. We turn on the tap, we wait for the water to warm up, and we let it run. Who has ever counted how many litres disappear in those two minutes? Nobody, I suspect. Never have we had so much clean water, yet rarely do we treat it with respect. Not only do we waste water at home, but we also waste the energy that heats it. Here is what I suggest: three simple habits. First, keep a bowl in the shower. Second, turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Third, repair every leak this week. Little did I know that three small habits would cut our bill by a third. Under no circumstances should we wait for a crisis, because water that has gone cannot be replaced. So tomorrow morning, turn off the tap, hold the bowl and feel what a difference it makes.

Think about the last time you left a tap running. Why did you do it? Because nobody ever told you that it matters. Seldom have we been asked to think about water, and rarely do we wonder where it goes. Not until a dry summer arrives do most of us notice. So let me give you three rules that cost nothing. First, take shorter showers. Second, use the washing machine only when it is full. Third, fix every leak at once. Little did my neighbours believe that these three rules could save a thousand litres a month, yet that is exactly what happened on our street. At no point should we say that one person cannot make a difference, because every street is made of people like you and me. So when you go home tonight, look at your tap, and ask yourself one thing: what will I change first?

feedback.es: Un buen centro de charla combina inversión, regla de tres y pregunta retórica, sin abusar del énfasis.

origin.text: Tema: el agua en casa. Escribe en inglés el centro de una charla (150–230 palabras): incluye al menos una inversión enfática (Never have we…, Rarely do we…, Not only do we… but…, Little did I know…), una regla de tres (anuncia «three habits», «three rules»… y enuméralas) y una pregunta retórica.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué hizo que la oradora comprendiera lo que significa un verano malo?

choices.text: Hearing her grandfather describe the worst summer of his life.
Reading a bill that showed how much water the house had used.
Standing by the dry river and seeing her grandfather's silence.

feedback.es: Fue al estar junto al río seco, viendo callado a su abuelo, cuando comprendió lo que significa un verano malo.

origin.audio: Not until I stood beside the dry river behind my grandfather's house did I understand what a bad summer means. Seldom had I seen him so quiet. Then he picked up some dust and let it fall through his hands, and little did I know that this silent moment would shape everything I do today. My grandfather never gave a speech in his life, yet that afternoon he taught me more than any lecture. Rarely do we connect a number on a bill with an empty river, but at no point should we separate them.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender la oradora con su última frase?

choices.text: That we should always link what we use at home to its effect on nature.
That water companies should print river levels on every customer's bill.
That anyone who checks a bill closely will soon waste far less water.

feedback.es: Pide no separar el número de la factura del río vacío: hay que vincular el consumo doméstico con sus consecuencias.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra el autor ante el uso excesivo de la inversión?

choices.text: Cautious: he advises against using inversion in any speech at all.
Critical: too many examples make a speech feel like a performance.
Neutral: the effect depends on how well the audience knows the speaker.

feedback.es: Advierte que una línea bien colocada refuerza un punto, pero diez seguidas muestran a un orador que actúa: postura crítica ante el exceso.

origin.text: Some speakers fall in love with inversion. Never have they been so pleased with themselves, and rarely do their audiences share the feeling. A single well-placed line can hammer home a point; ten in a row only tell listeners that the speaker is performing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No gastes saliva en un argumento débil.»

answer.text: Do not waste your breath on a weak argument

feedback.es: Waste your breath describe el esfuerzo inútil; on introduce aquello en lo que no merece la pena gastarlo.

prompt.es: Reescribe con Not only: escribió el discurso y también lo pronunció.

answer.text: Not only did she write the speech, but she also delivered it.
accepted: Not only did she write the speech, but she also delivered it.
Not only did she write the speech, but she also gave it.
Not only did she write the speech, but she delivered it too.

feedback.es: Not only abre la frase, did va antes de she, y la segunda parte añade also o too.
